findings.title: Compare-and-set needs decode then encode to give back the exact stored JSON
findings.body: `expected` comes from `decodeProviderThreadPayload(row.payload_json)` (ProjectionStore.ts:3924), and here it is re-encoded and compared byte for byte with the stored `payload_json`. That works for rows written by the current code, which stores `encodeProviderThreadPayload(event.payload)` (ProjectionStore.ts:2204, 2233). A row last written by an older schema version may not survive the round trip unchanged: a field with a decoding default, a renamed or reordered key, or a stripped excess key would all break it. For such a row every attempt in `writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents` (ProviderSessionManager.ts:846-883) fails. The only trace is the `release-roster-conflict` warning, and the thread keeps showing Waiting, the bug this PR fixes. Is the provider-thread JSON schema guaranteed to round-trip canonically for old rows? If not, comparing against `parse(row)` re-encoded, or against the `pendingBackgroundTasks` field only, would avoid permanent mismatches.

contracts.action: Release reads the background rosters of the released session's provider threads
contracts.equivalent_path: Runtime-request cleanup reads its cutoff in removeLiveEntry while holding the request permit
contracts.before_after: The rosters are read after removeLiveEntry and before the subscribers end and the scope closes, and they are written after closeScopeWithin, together with the session and request records.
contracts.visible_effect: The provider-thread.updated event is published through commitThenPublish, so the thread drops out of Waiting.
contracts.failure_mode: A failed read is caught and logged, and an empty list is returned (ProviderSessionManager.ts:821-827). That roster is not cleared and is never retried.
contracts.open_question: Can the event pump still persist provider-thread.updated for this runtime between the roster read and the scope close? If it can, a task started in that window is never cleared.

contracts.action: writeIfProviderThreadUnchanged compares the stored payload_json with the re-encoded expected row
contracts.before_after: The comparison and the append happen inside one commitThenPublish transaction, and events are published only when committed.
contracts.visible_effect: The roster disappears once the write commits.
contracts.failure_mode: On a mismatch it returns committed:false. The caller tries 3 times and then logs a warning, so the roster stays.

contracts.action: The backgroundTasksEndWithProcess option is read by the session manager
contracts.visible_effect: Only Claude and Muse set it. When it is unset (OpenCode and others), release leaves the rosters as they are.

contracts.action: Release records are retried after a failed write and now include the roster clear
contracts.before_after: Every attempt filters by task id against the row as it is read now, so removing the same tasks again changes nothing.
contracts.failure_mode: When the comparison keeps failing, the roster helper logs and returns without an error, so a conflict never triggers the outer retry.

summary:
I reviewed all 7 files in this part. The change does what the title says. When a Claude or Muse session is released by detach, idle timeout or manual close, its provider threads' background-task rosters are cleared, so the thread stops showing Waiting. Server shutdown is skipped, as is any runtime that doesn't opt in (OpenCode). The write is a compare-and-set against the stored `payload_json`, and it is retried up to 3 times.

The ordering looks right. The rosters are read after the entry leaves the live map and before the scope closes. Tasks that a replacement session reports later are kept, because they're filtered by task id and guarded by the compare-and-set. The roster write also goes through `retryReleaseRecords` without trouble, because removing the same task ids twice does nothing the second time.

Two weak spots, both low/medium confidence:
- **Older rows may never clear.** The compare-and-set only matches if re-encoding the decoded row gives back exactly the stored JSON. For a row written by an older schema version that may never happen, and the roster would then quietly stay put after a warning log.
- **Tasks started late are missed.** The rosters are read before the scope closes. A task the dying process reports in that gap isn't cleared, and whether the event pump still writes provider-thread updates at that point is unconfirmed.

The tests cover these paths: detach release, idle release, opting out, a replacement reporting a task mid-release, and a write that lands between the read and the compare-and-set.
